$comment: Budget for the boot payload: the entry chunk plus its static-import
closure. That is the JavaScript a phone must download, parse and compile
before the app renders anything, so it is the number that decides how
slow bb feels on mobile.
Chunks behind a dynamic import are deliberately not counted. Moving code
behind React.lazy or import() is the fix this budget exists to encourage.
On 2026-09-25 the SplitWorkspaceRoute limits rose by 2 KiB raw and
256 bytes brotli for sanitized HTML video support in thread Markdown.
On 2026-09-25 the SplitWorkspaceRoute raw and brotli limits rose
by 1 KiB and 256 bytes respectively for secondary-panel pixel minimums,
container resize handling, and
late-mounted panel size synchronization.
On 2026-09-25 both SplitWorkspaceRoute limits rose another 2 KiB for
machine enrollment command status and selected-machine sidebar placement.
On 2026-09-26 the SplitWorkspaceRoute raw limit rose 0.5 KiB for
nested worktree group alignment. No new dependencies enter the route.
Both boot limits were temporarily raised 5% on 2026-09-21 to restore
headroom while reducing the measured boot payload by at least 10%.
These allowances leave room for normal shell feature work and build
noise, tight enough that a barrel regression cannot hide inside it. Lower
them when a change wins headroom. Raising one is a deliberate decision
that needs a reason in the pull request, not a routine edit.
On 2026-09-22 bb's built-in sidebar navigation moved into the bundled
Navigation plugin, which took @dnd-kit off the boot path. The boot limits
dropped by the full win (about 109 KB raw, 27 KB brotli). The thread
route's queued-message reorder still statically imports @dnd-kit, so the
SplitWorkspaceRoute limits rose by the code that moved there (about 64 KB
raw, 20 KB brotli). The total budget went down.
On 2026-09-29 sidebar footer customization moved behind React.lazy.
Its static import had put @dnd-kit back on the boot path on 2026-09-26.
The boot limits dropped by the full win (61,053 bytes raw, 15,730
brotli), and the @dnd-kit packages joined forbiddenBootPackages. The
thread route's queued-message reorder still loads @dnd-kit statically, so
the SplitWorkspaceRoute closure grew by 49,568 bytes raw and 14,918
brotli within its existing limits, which already assumed @dnd-kit there.
On 2026-09-23 the SplitWorkspaceRoute brotli limit rose 2 KB. main sat
0.1 KB under it, and a change that shrank the raw closure by 29 bytes
still moved the compressed closure 0.6 KB through minifier renaming and
chunk-hash churn alone. The raw limit did not change.
There is deliberately no per-chunk limit. Parse and compile cost scales
with the total bytes on the boot path, not with how they are divided, so
splitting one boot chunk into two would satisfy a per-chunk cap while
making the page slightly slower for the extra request.
forbiddenBootPackages is the more important half. These packages are all
large and all needed only after a user action (open a diff, focus the
composer, render math). Each one reached the boot path through a barrel
re-export rather than a direct import, which type checking cannot catch,
so the check names them explicitly.
onDemandPackages goes one step further than the boot path: each package
maps to its gate, the source module a dynamic import() resolves to. The
package may appear only in the static import closure of that gate's chunk.
Any other chunk whose static closure reaches the package fails the check.
KaTeX is the example: markdown-preview is a static import of the thread
route, so a static rehype-katex import would put ~64 KB brotli of math
renderer in front of every thread's first paint even though almost no
message contains $$ math.
routeClosures ratchets page journeys: the union of the static-import
closures of a page's lazy chunks minus the boot chunks, the JavaScript
between 'app shell painted' and 'page content painted'. ThreadPage and
NewThreadPage decide how slow bb feels on a phone after boot. Their
forbiddenPackages are the diff engine, math, file tree and terminal code
that only a user action needs.
The composer (tiptap/prosemirror) is visible on both pages and is allowed.
Run `node scripts/why-eager.mjs --from=views/SplitWorkspaceRoute.tsx <package>`
to print the static chain that pulled a package into the route.
On 2026-09-29 the second split wave moved terminal output, queued messages,
model-menu contents and command-palette contents behind demand/intent gates.
The panel policy audit also removed blanket idle preloading and gated first
panel/browser mounts. Compared with fc92e220a6, the integrated changes saved
13,894 boot raw / 3,514 boot brotli bytes and
175,237 thread-route raw / 41,117 thread-route brotli bytes.
All four limits dropped by those net measured savings; none were raised.

ProseMirror in blockquote, and separates thread detail, plugin ThreadChat,
and Markdown HTML from the workspace route. The route limits drop by

HTML bytes warm on idle without importing; actual thread visits still load

to restore CI headroom after mobile recent-thread long-press actions.
A separate follow-up will reduce the route payload and ratchet these

implementations from the shipped app. Both workspace limits returned
to their values before the temporary 5% increase. This reduction removes

prosemirror-dropcursor and prosemirror-gapcursor are forbidden on boot

On 2026-10-05 microphone input preferences joined the composer and both
SplitWorkspaceRoute limits temporarily rose 5%. The composer now loads

On 2026-10-05 route closures became page journeys. ThreadPage is the
workspace route plus ThreadDetailView's static imports, and NewThreadPage is
the workspace route plus RootComposeView's. Each counts the JavaScript a
page waits for beyond the boot payload, so moving code between the route and
a page's own chunk no longer changes the measured total.
On 2026-10-05 an audit cut the boot payload from 1492.0 KB to 1358.5 KB
(sideEffects on client-core, thread-view and core-ui; sonner and the server
move view after first paint) and ThreadPage from 1880.0 KB to 1807.2 KB,
mostly by loading the new-thread view on demand. The boot limits stay,
leaving about 15% raw headroom, and both journey limits are set 25% above
their measured sizes (20% headroom) so ordinary feature work does not hit
them every week. The forbidden-package and split-boundary guards catch
structural regressions.
